text: The tiny ridges on your coins were put there to stop thieves!
Because coins used to be made of real silver, and people would shave them.
They snipped a thin sliver off the edge. Do that to a hundred coins, melt the slivers, and you have free silver!
This was called clipping, and you could be put to death for it.
So in sixteen sixty-two, England put a pattern on the edge of its coins.
Now a clipped coin was easy to spot!
But old coins were everywhere, so in sixteen ninety-six, England remade all its money.
And the man hunting the cheaters was Isaac Newton!
His biggest target was a forger named William Chaloner, who even faked the edges.
Newton questioned the witnesses himself, and Chaloner was hanged.
Today's coins are not silver. But the ridges stayed, and they help blind people tell coins apart by touch!
So those ridges are a three-hundred-year-old anti-theft trick!
